rounds.proof_sketch: grid.y = ceil(inner_size/256). For shape [16,256,256] with dim=1: inner_size=256, grid.y=1, so blockIdx.y∈{0}. Since blockIdx.z=0 always (default), both expressions equal threadIdx.x. Distinguishability requires dim=0 (inner_size=65536, grid.y=256), which is a config change.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes blockIdx.y to blockIdx.z in the inner_idx calculation. However, with the fixed input shape [16,256,256] and dim=1, the kernel launches with grid.y=1. When grid.y=1, blockIdx.y can only be 0, which equals the default blockIdx.z value of 0. Thus both original and mutated code compute inner_idx = 0*256 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x. The mutation is only distinguishable when grid.y > 1, requiring inner_size > 256, which requires either a different input shape or dim=0. Neither is allowed under the testing contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Requires dim=0 (config change) to make inner_size=65536, yielding grid.y=256 where blockIdx.y≠blockIdx.z for most threads.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should include configuration-space mutations (varying dim, block_size, etc.) alongside value mutations. For index-swapping mutations, ensure test configurations exercise multi-block launches in ALL grid dimensions that appear in index expressions.
